t: None of the money appropriated hereby shall be used to make any payment on any lease purchase contract for jet airplanes to be used by the Federal Aviation Administration wherein the total cost of the lease payments plus the amount needed to exercise the purchase option exceeds the purchase price of the aircraft (which would have been charged where the aircraft to be purchased by normal appropriations) by more than 20%.

fable.w: This is an appropriations limitation restricting the use of funds for certain FAA lease-purchase contracts for jet airplanes. The tempting reading is that a lease purchase contract involves an outside company, but a contract is a procurement transaction, not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. The section provides for no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: None of the money appropriated hereby shall be used to make any payment on any lease purchase contract for jet airplanes to be used by the Federal Aviation Administration

opus.w: This section limits how appropriated funds may be spent on lease-purchase contracts for FAA jet airplanes. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The outside contractor in a lease-purchase deal is a party to a contract, and contracts are explicitly excluded from participation, so the tempting reading fails.
opus.s: None of the money appropriated hereby shall be used to make any payment on any lease purchase contract for jet airplanes to be used by the Federal Aviation Administration

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a financial limit on lease-purchase contracts for jet airplanes. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as manufacturers, the public, or state governments) in the decision-making process. It is purely a restriction on the use of appropriated funds.
qwen_chat.s: None of the money appropriated hereby shall be used to make any payment on any lease purchase contract for jet airplanes to be used by the Federal Aviation Administration wherein the total cost of the lease payments plus the amount needed to exercise the purchase option exceeds the purchase price of the aircraft (which would have been charged where the aircraft to be purchased by normal appropriations) by more than 20%.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "lease purchase contract" implies a process where outside parties (aircraft manufacturers) participate in negotiations. However, the text itself only sets a financial cap on what the government will pay; it does not describe any procedural requirement for consultation, comment periods, hearings, or advisory boards involving outside parties. It is a budgetary restriction, not a participation mechanism.
